reply.thought: The first step is to check the refunds reported by Alpha Co against the system's records using list_refunds(). This will confirm if the refunds match what was reported before proceeding to calculate and record payouts.

The system's refund list confirms records for order_id 213 and 214. Alpha Co reported refunds for these two orders, and also reported a failure for order_id 211. The system's list of refunds does not show any record for order_id 211, which aligns with the failure report from Alpha Co. Since the reported and recorded refunds match (only 213 and 214 are present and confirmed), I can proceed to check the net balance for all customers involved.

I have the list of orders. The customers involved are 'acme', 'birch', and 'cobalt'. I need to use net_balance(customer) for each unique customer to get their final payout amount. I will start with 'acme'.
I have the net balance for 'acme'. Next, I will check the net balance for the next unique customer, 'birch'.
I have the net balance for 'birch'. Next, I will check the net balance for the last unique customer, 'cobalt'.

I have successfully retrieved the net balances for all customers: acme (48125), birch (67298), and cobalt (46961). Since the refunds matched and I have all the required balances, I will now record the payouts in the order they were calculated to minimize risk, starting with 'acme'.
Payout for 'acme' recorded successfully. Next, I will record the payout for 'birch'.
Payout for 'birch' recorded successfully. Finally, I will record the payout for 'cobalt'.
